Q1: Methyl tert-butyl ether (MTBE) exhibits known significant hazards for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive toxicity (CMR), inhalation (IHL), and oral exposure (ORL), all classified at Tier 1. It also shows an expanded perspective of potential hazards for endocrine disruption (EDC) and dermal/eye exposure (SKN) at Tier 2. While environmental hazards (ENV) are deemed low/moderate (Tier 3), data for organ and systemic hazards (OGN) are currently deficient (Tier 4), indicating an area of unknown risk.
Q2: Methyl tert-butyl ether is identified on several significant lists of concern, including the TEDX list as a potential endocrine disruptor, and is regulated under the Safe Drinking Water Act. It is also recognized as a Hazardous Air Pollutant and is part of the National Air Toxics Assessment, further appearing on the "Substitute In Now" list, suggesting recognized hazards may prompt its replacement.
Q3: Methyl tert-butyl ether is extensively characterized, evidenced by over 22,000 scientific literature references, which is far above the median for studied chemicals. Its molecular formula (C5H12O) is precisely defined, and its classification as a "Small Molecule" confirms it is a well-understood substance rather than an incompletely defined material or UVCB. While most hazard areas are thoroughly assessed, there is a data deficiency regarding organ and systemic hazards.
